cells.title: POST /api/orders creates an order
cells.markdown:
Send a **real** `POST /api/orders` for 3 widgets.

- Expect status **201 Created**
- The body echoes the order with `status` = `created`
cells.display:
node http-step.mjs --step AC1 --method POST \
  --url http://127.0.0.1:4318/api/orders \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --body '{"item":"widget","qty":3}' \
  --expect-status 201 --expect-json status=created --expect-json item=widget

cells.title: Creating an order writes an OrderCreated log line
cells.markdown:
Remember where `app.log` ends, create a **gadget** order, then show only the *new* lines matching `OrderCreated id=… item=gadget`.

The inner request has its own step (`AC2-request`); the cell's verdict comes from the outer `AC2` log check.
cells.display:
node log-step.mjs --step AC2 --file app.log \
  --pattern "OrderCreated id=ord-\d+ item=gadget" \
  --run node http-step.mjs --step AC2-request --method POST \
    --url http://127.0.0.1:4318/api/orders \
    --body '{"item":"gadget","qty":2}' --expect-status 201

cells.title: POST /api/refunds accepts a refund
cells.markdown:
Request a refund for order `ord-1000`. The criterion says the API answers **202 Accepted** with `status` = `accepted`.

This example API does not implement refunds, so this cell is expected to **FAIL** — and the failure is shown, not hidden.
cells.display:
node http-step.mjs --step AC3 --method POST \
  --url http://127.0.0.1:4318/api/refunds \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --body '{"orderId":"ord-1000","amount":12.5}' \
  --expect-status 202 --expect-json status=accepted
